chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Basir said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about something of the fixed shares (of inheritance), so he said to me, 'Shall I bring out for you the Book of Ali (peace be upon him)?' I said, 'The Book of Ali (peace be upon him) has not worn out.' He said, 'O Abu Muhammad, indeed the Book of Ali (peace be upon him) does not wear out.' So he brought it out, and behold, it was a noble book. In it was: 'If a man died and left his paternal uncle and his maternal uncle,' he said, 'For the paternal uncle two-thirds, and for the maternal uncle one-third.'
ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance share of paternal and maternal uncles according to the Book of Ali?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the authority of a specific book attributed to Imam Ali (peace be upon him), asserting its enduring preservation ('la yandaras') against claims of textual corruption. The narration establishes a distinct Shia inheritance ruling where, in the absence of closer heirs, the paternal uncle receives two-thirds and the maternal uncle one-third, highlighting the unique jurisprudential derivation from the Ahl al-Bayt's transmitted knowledge.
